dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Friend! That we should meet means that fate has surely smiled upon you. Oh, how I—

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Didn't you go bust?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Ah, friend, how your words wound my very soul! That lesson I was taught was sore enough. Shall we not let bygones be bygones?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: I've been working hard at the wharf since I ran myself out of house and home, and happened upon a business opportunity while I was at it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why yes, I'm familiar with your business sense...

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Oh, come now. Don't say that. I've earned a little money since, and am now completely free of debt.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Either way, this business is a sure bet, the long travel distance to Sumeru notwithstanding.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: As most know, Sumeru is all rainforest and desert. Other than mushrooms, all goods are welcome there. I'm sure you understand my meaning, don't you, friend?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: The rules are the same as before. I'll collect some common goods from other lands, and send them on to Sumeru. And since we're old partners, I'll give you a special price, too!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Guess we'll give it another go...

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Haha! So, this is how we'll do it—

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Hello there, friend. It's been a while, hasn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hello, Liben. How have you been?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Well, I'd say that I've found the proverbial light at the end of the tunnel at last. After returning from Sumeru previously, I did a quick cargo run to Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Since things weren't looking so hot in Sumeru, I decided to try my luck in Fontaine instead.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: I was just going to observe the market a little, you know, and if I made my capital back? Well, you wouldn't see me complaining.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: I never could have been prepared for how much the locals there loved Inazuman goods.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: The goods I had on me and couldn't sell in other countries, such as the Ms. Hina merchandise, actually sold out.

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: The people of Fontaine love messing about with mechanical devices, and relatively few, by contrast, spend time developing such trinkets as these.

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: I suppose that's the scarcity principle for you.

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: Hahaha. Well, if it didn't look like dark clouds were gathering there too, I'd have made a few more trips for sure.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What's going on over there?

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: Well, things just feel oppressive and dangerous... You know, like a storm is about to break out.

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: The locals were pretty antsy... Said judgment was soon to come, or something like that.

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: I'd suggest you refrain from going there lest you get yourself into trouble that you can't easily get out of.

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: Well, then our arrangement shall be the same as always.

choices.text: So Ms. Hina got to show her quality, eh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can you run me through your background again?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: I'm Liben, and once upon a time I sold curios.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: I've been doing good business recently.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What kind of business are you talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Ah, it's simple. You see, you just need to find me a few basic everyday items, cooking ingredients and the like, and then you trade them with me for a Box o' Marvels that are stuffed full of all kinds of nice little treasures.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Keep in mind that I've filled these Boxes o' Marvels with the fortune I made in my time as a seller of curios. There's no booby prizes to be found here, and I treat all my customers the same.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Why box them up and turn it into a lucky draw, you ask?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: What can I say, people like a gift box. It just makes everyone a little more inclined to get involved.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How are you going to earn any Mora like this?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Something like this... Let's worry about it when the time comes.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: If worse comes to worst, I'll take a trip to Natlan next time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can you tell me about your background again?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: I'm Liben, and once upon a time, I sold curios.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: I've been doing good business recently.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Before that, I ran the Nod-Krai trade route, hoping to make myself a small fortune.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: But... I'm still here, so I'm sure you know how that turned out!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What kind of business are you talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Simple. You find me a few basic everyday items, cooking ingredients and the like, and then you trade them with me for a Box o' Marvels, full of all kinds of nice little treasures.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Keep in mind that I've filled these Boxes o' Marvels with the fortune I made in my time as a seller of curios. There's no booby prizes to be found here, and I treat all my customers the same.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Why box them up and turn it into a lucky draw, you ask?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: What can I say, people like a gift box. It just makes everyone a little more inclined to get involved.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do you earn any money like this?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Hmm, fair point. Perhaps I should explore business opportunities in Natlan next time after all, eh?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Or maybe hire a few people for protection and make another trip to Nod-Krai, that might work too...

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: To be honest, though, I'm getting pretty tired...

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Guess I'll take a break before making any more plans!

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Hello, friend. It's been a long time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Liben, I trust you've been well?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Life is full of triumphs and setbacks. I've grown used to it, you know. A small illness is nothing to write home about, and minor losses are just part of the game.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: So I suppose you could say I've been well enough, ha!

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: How about you, friend?

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: That's marvelous to hear!

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: I am overjoyed today, because I have run into you once again, my friend!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Anything interesting happening lately?

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: Don't you think I ought to head to Natlan and seek out new business opportunities? Seize the day and strike while the iron's hot?

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: Hahaha, I don't actually want to go to Natlan this time.

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: A few days ago, I accidentally fell into a hole and spent the whole night staring at the stars.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That definitely doesn't count as having been "well" lately...

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: Anyway, I was rescued by a passing adventurer, and didn't even get hungry down there! All's well that ends well, am I right?

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: Looking up at the stars at night, I couldn't help but wonder... What lies beyond this world?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Uh... Endless distance, and endless worlds.

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: You think so too, friend?

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: I was thinking how, what if every single star was actually a sun, and each of those suns had a planet orbiting it that we could visit?

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: Or what if we could even visit every single star themselves? After all, they just give off light, maybe they aren't even that hot?

choices.text: The nights there would be quite bright. You couldn't sleep with that much light.

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: Oh, that's true. Then it would be enough just to go look. Though no one could live there like that, so I guess there wouldn't be any business opportunities.

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: Back to the matter at hand, our old deal is still on, right? No changes?

choices.text: Trying to trailblaze a new trade route?

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: Do the nations up in the sky use Mora too? But if those places are lit up all day long, then nobody can live there, right?

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: ...Really?

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: Hey there, friend! It's been a while!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It sure has, Liben!

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: Hehe, enthusiastic as ever, I see... I wonder, how changed a man am I?

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: That's good. I mean, I almost didn't make it back this time.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Did you try your luck in Natlan?

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: Nope! I heard that things there were tense, so I deliberately avoided it and went to Nod-Krai instead.

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: Have you been there?

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: No? Well, I guess I can tell you about it then.

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: Nod-Krai is in the southernmost part of Snezhnaya, where people from all over Teyvat gather. Those not in the know would think that opportunities to get rich are everywhere there.

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: It's only after you get there that you realize that it's a wild place that plays by its own rules.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Its own rules?

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: Let me put it this way: Before I even set foot in the city, I was robbed by a group of vagrants — taking advantage of my ignorance about the place.

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: Courts of law, Knights of Favonius... There's none of that there. Someone just told me to visit the Voynich Guild.

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: Said the Guild was the strongest force in the area and that they might be able to get me justice.

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: I was only half-convinced at first, so imagine my surprise when the Guild folks not only hauled all my goods back — they even bought everything off me, too. Totally amazing, right?

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: I was so happy to see that much Mora, I counted it all up several times!

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: "I've done it! Woohoo!"

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: Ugh... I don't even wanna talk about it. When I left the city again, I ran into another band of vagrants, who robbed me of every Mora — not a single coin was spared.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: They must've already had their eye on you back in the city...

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: *sigh* That's me, Liben, for you! Only the grandest peaks and deepest troughs of life! Anyway, I'm not going back there — not for a while at least.

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: So yeah, stay on your toes if you're going to Nod-Krai, and don't let just anyone know that you're holding onto a big bag of Mora.

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: So, I trust that our deal's still on, then?

choices.text: You keep your guard up too, Liben.
What kind of place is that?
